draft.title: The Eureka Stockade
card: In 1854 many miners at Ballarat, in the colony of Victoria, were angry about the cost of the licence they had to buy to dig for gold. They had to pay it whether or not they found any gold.
Miners also had no vote, so they could not elect anyone to speak for them in the colony's government. Police checks for licences added to the anger.

In December 1854 miners built a rough stockade, a wall of timber, and swore to defend their rights. Soldiers and police attacked it early one morning and crushed the protest in a short fight. Both miners and soldiers were killed.
Many people did not accept the harsh response, and the miners who were put on trial were found not guilty. Soon afterwards the licence was replaced and miners won the right to vote.
draft.remember: Miners protested costly licences and having no vote. They lost the fight but won changes soon after.

a.q: Which pair of grievances led the Ballarat miners to protest in 1854?
opts: A costly licence and no vote
Low wool prices and high taxes on trade
Fear of Chinese miners and a lack of land
Bad pay from mine owners and long working hours
a.why: The miners had to pay for a licence whether or not they found gold, and they had no vote to change the rules. The other pairs mix in ideas from other parts of the gold rush story, such as hostility to Chinese miners, which was not the cause of this protest.
a.clue: Think about what miners paid for and what they could not do at the ballot box.

b.q: Soldiers crushed the Eureka stockade in a short fight. Why do historians still treat it as a success for the miners?
opts: Miners soon won the vote and the licence was replaced
The miners drove the soldiers out of Ballarat
The government shut down all the goldfields
The leaders of the protest were all found guilty
b.why: The miners lost the fight itself, but many people were shocked by the response. Soon afterwards the licence was replaced and miners won the vote. The tempting wrong option is that the miners won the fight, but the card says the soldiers crushed the stockade.
b.clue: Look at what happened after the fight, not during it.

a.best: A costly licence and no vote

b.best: Miners soon won the vote and the licence was replaced

check.summary: No problems found. The facts check out: the 1854 Ballarat protest, licence hunts, the December attack on the stockade, the acquittals, and the licence being replaced by the miner's right with the vote.
